newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end up sharply, more data on tap.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end up sharply, more data on tap.

text.p: U.S. debt futures rallied to more than one-month highs after weaker-than-expected economic news this morning and ended sharply higher.
June Treasury bond futures soared to the upper 108-00 handle in fast market trading and held gains for the rest of the session, drifting up to a new daily high of 109-00 late.
"The first hour was good volume," one T-bond futures trader said. The rest of the session was spent "establishing a range at higher levels."
Traders said the soft March durable goods orders and small gain in wage costs spooked weak short position holders early.

First-quarter ECI rose 0.6 pct versus the forecast for up 0.9 percent and the 0.8-percent gain in the previous report. March durable goods orders fell 3.0 percent overall and fell 2.6 percent ex-defense. The forecast had been for unchanged overall and a 0.1-percent drop in ex-defense orders.

"A lot of short-covering dominated the trade," one Eurodollar trader said. "I think the data probably reduced the odds (for a May 20 rate hike) down from 70 to 80 percent to 40 or 50 percent," he said.
"Everything just had to be adjusted accordingly," he said.
Traders noted that the week holds much more data.
Some traders said more shorts were in the market, and further weak data this week could jar them loose.

On tap for Wednesday are preliminary first-quarter growth and New York and Chicago purchasing management surveys. GDP was forecast at 4.1 percent, from 3.8 percent in the previous report. April Chicago purchasing managers was forecast at 56.2, from 57.5 in the previous report.
National Association of Purchasing Management data takes center stage on Thursday, with April non-farm payrolls Friday.
"There's still important news out this week, but today was signficant," the Euro trader said.
While some traders said the morning's data questions the certainty of a Fed hike in May, others said more proof of a not-so-robust economy was needed,
"We're going to keep an open mind," another Euro broker said. "We've got a lot of data out this week."

At the close, June T-bonds were up 1-17/32 to 108-30/32, 10-year notes rose 31/32 to 106-19/32, September T-bills were up 0.185 at 94.445, September Eurodollars were up 0.180 at 93.875 and December Eurodollars were 0.220 higher at 93.615.
